description: Discriminator: a persisted vote must not be replaced by a different vote in the same term. One voter node is created by the package's own NewRaft over the real NetworkTransport with a socket-free StreamLayer; a heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries from a deposed leader carrying term 6 is held inside that node's StableStore CurrentTerm write, and while the write is held a candidate of term 7 asks for a vote, which the node grants because its adopted term is still 1. Releasing the held write publishes term 6, below the term the node just voted in, and the node's own election then proposes term 7 again. Observation: the durable vote record, the pair (LastVoteTerm, LastVoteCand), is read before and after the election and the asserted field is whether the second persisted vote's term differs from the first's. Control: the prefix keeps the ordinary behaviour visible - the first vote is granted only while the node's adopted term is 1, the stale heartbeat is rejected on every read after the release because its term is then below the published one, and the record's candidate changes only when the node persists its own vote.

harness.description: TestAssuranceVoteRecordTermReuse: stale-term heartbeat held across a higher-term vote grant, then the node's own election
semantic_changes: StreamLayer is replaced by an in-process net.Pipe fabric; NetworkTransport, its heartbeat classification, the SetHeartbeatHandler registration, requestVote, appendEntries and electSelf are the target's own code.

StableStore is an InmemStore wrapper that holds exactly one CurrentTerm write inside SetUint64. This is a latency injection on an injected dependency; no term comparison, vote rule or write order in the target is changed.

The harness reads the durable vote record directly from the StableStore instead of inferring it from RPC responses, and it reads the pair twice before accepting it so a concurrent election cannot tear the observation.
No target file is modified; the harness adds one external test file to the captured package.

legality.derivation: requestVote writes the durable vote record through persistVote and refuses a second, different vote in a term it has already voted in, by comparing the recorded term and candidate with the request (s-raft-vote-record); electSelf instead persists a self-vote for its proposed term unconditionally, before it sends any vote request (s-raft-elect-self); both paths publish the term through setCurrentTerm, which stores StableStore before the in-memory value (s-raft-set-current-term, s-state-term-atomic). A heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries is handled by Raft.processHeartbeat on the transport connection goroutine (s-raft-process-heartbeat, s-net-fastpath), it adopts a greater term before anything else (s-raft-append-term), and its own state transition clears the known leader (s-raft-set-state), so a delayed StableStore write from that path can leave the published term below one the node has already voted in. electSelf derives its proposed term from the published term plus one, so a published term that has dropped by one causes the next election to propose exactly the term the node already voted in and to overwrite the record with its own candidate.
legality.applicability: The node holds a committed configuration with itself as a voter, pre-vote is disabled because the substitute transport does not implement WithPreVote, and the only RPCs in the prefix are one stale heartbeat, one higher-term RequestVote and the node's own outbound vote requests, which the substitute fabric cannot deliver to a live peer.
unresolved: the witness shows the local vote record being reused; whether a second leader in that term becomes possible depends on other voters' records and is not part of this prefix
whether the intended repair belongs in the term update path or in electSelf's unconditional persistVote
conflicts: the vote-granting path refuses a second different vote in the same term from its durable record while the candidate path persists a self-vote for its proposed term without consulting that record, so the one-vote-per-term rule is enforced on only one of the two paths that write the record
alternatives: the rule could be read as binding only the grant path, in which case the record's overwrite is harmless; the check's premise is that the record, not the response, is what makes at most one leader per term possible

grounding.derivation: The result event reports the vote record that is in effect when the record's candidate changes after the release, and the admission event reports the record written by the granted higher-term vote, so the pair describes the two persisted votes the node has made. The applicability condition requires the second record's candidate to differ from the first, which is what makes a shared term a violation of the one-vote-per-term rule rather than the harmless re-grant that requestVote performs without writing again (s-raft-vote-record); the second write in this prefix is the self-vote electSelf persists for its proposed term (s-raft-elect-self) after the published term was dropped by the delayed write (s-raft-set-current-term).
grounding.applicability: Same node and same prefix as the harness; the diagnostic fields (state, term writes, granted flag) are reported beside the compared pair.
unresolved: whether a second leader in the shared term can follow from the same defect on other voters

observable_properties.description: For a second persisted vote whose candidate differs from the first, the term it is recorded under must differ from the term of the first vote; equality means the node has recorded two different votes in one term, which is the local condition Raft's election safety rests on. The predicate is the invariant itself rather than a proxy: the compared terms come from the two durable records, and applicability already restricts the comparison to records whose candidates differ, so a legitimate re-grant of the same candidate is never judged.

uncertainties: The witness establishes the local vote-record violation only; two leaders in one term additionally require the other voters' records to be corrupted the same way, which this prefix does not contain.

The delayed StableStore write is an injection on an injected dependency, exercised through the documented transport callback; the interleaving it exposes follows from the entry point running off the main goroutine, which the plan cites rather than re-derives here.

The second vote is caused by the node's own election timer, so its timing is bounded by HeartbeatTimeout and ElectionTimeout rather than being instantaneous; the harness waits for the record to change and reads the pair twice before accepting it.
The identity fields are fixed harness labels for a single node and single prefix, so correlation is unique but not discriminating across multiple operations.
Only the vote-record path is observed: no leader is elected and no log is replicated in this prefix.
